 Lincoln is recalling 11,623 hybrid crossovers because a transmission defect can drop the vehicle into neutral without warning while it's moving. The recall covers select 2026-2027 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid models and 2027 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid models, and the fix addresses a part failure that cuts power to the wheels mid-drive, raising the odds of a rear-end collision.

 Ford traced the problem to the Integrated Park Module, a component inside the transmission's park lock actuator system. Owners should check their VIN now, even though full repairs are still rolling out at dealerships. 
 Corrosion Inside The Transmission Is Triggering False Neutral Commands
 Front 3/4 action shot of 2026 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid driving Lincoln 
 The root cause comes down to a manufacturing change that went wrong. A specific anti-rust oil used during assembly can seep onto the printed circuit board inside the Integrated Park Module. Over time, that oil breaks down the board's protective conformal coating, which lets corrosion spread across the rotary sensor circuit and a capacitor.
 As corrosion builds, the rotary sensor's output voltage starts to drop. When that signal degrades enough, the powertrain control system misreads it as a fault and commands the transmission into neutral, even with the vehicle in motion. Ford says the same failure can also leave a parked vehicle unable to shift out of Park. Drivers may get an early warning first: a wrench-shaped malfunction light paired with a "Service Vehicle Soon" or "Shifting System Error" message on the dash.
 Which Nautilus And Corsair Models Are Affected
 2027 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid front-quarter Lincoln 
 The recall covers 11,560 Nautilus Hybrids from the 2026 and 2027 model years built between September 9, 2025, and August 6, 2026, along with 63 Corsair Hybrids from the 2027 model year. Ford isn't aware of any crashes, fires, or injuries tied to the defect, but the automaker has logged 15 US warranty claims, one US field report, and one US customer report as of late September. According to NHTSA documentation, Ford estimates 100% of the vehicles covered by the recall are actually affected, not just a subset flagged as a precaution. 
 Ford opened its investigation after field reports of wrench warning lights surfaced on hybrids using the same HF55 transmission, including two separate warranty claims describing a loss of power on 2026 Ford Edge hybrids. Testing in September confirmed the anti-rust oil swap at the module supplier was the culprit, and Ford's Field Review Committee signed off on the recall on October 13.
 What Nautilus And Corsair Owners Should Do Right Now
 Front 3/4 shot of 2026 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid parked Lincoln 
 Affected VINs became searchable on NHTSA.gov on October 26. Because vehicles weren't built in strict VIN order, Lincoln owners shouldn't assume they're in the clear without checking directly, either through NHTSA's site or by calling a local dealer. Ford will mail interim notification letters starting November 2 to alert owners to the hazard, with a second letter to follow once dealers have enough Integrated Park Modules in stock to perform the swap.
 The fix itself is straightforward and free: dealers will replace the IPM with an updated unit built without the problematic anti-rust oil and loaded with the latest software. Owners with questions can reach Ford customer service at 1-866-436-7332 and reference recall campaign number 26S75. Given that a wrench light and "Shifting System Error" message can show up before anything more serious happens, that dashboard warning is worth treating as a go-to-the-dealer-now signal rather than something to put off.
